 Judgment
Dated this the 9th day of October, 2025 1.

The Opposite Party No.1 / the Deputy Director of ESI Corporation before the Employees'
Insurance Court is the appellant.

The Application was filed by the 1 st respondent/applicant when the applicant received a notice demanding payment of a contribution of Rs.45,045/- for the period from 01.10.2012 to 30.04.2013 with respect to the establishment 'Hotel Nadan Ruchi'.

His contention was that the establishment, 'Nadan Ruchi Restaurant', which was run by him, and the establishment 'Hotel Nadan Ruchi', run by the 2nd respondent/3rd opposite party, are two separate and distinct establishments.

The application was allowed by the impugned Order holding that the establishment, 'Nadan Ruchi Restaurant' of the applicant and the establishment 'Hotel Nadan Ruchi' run by the 3rd opposite party are separate and distinct entities and directing the ESI corporation to refund the payment made by the applicant for the period from 01.10.2012 to 30.04.2013.
I heard Sri. Renil Anto Kandamkulathy, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant, and the learned counsel for the 1st respondent.
3. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that even though the 3rd opposite party was there in the application, the 3rd opposite party is not shown in the impugned Order.
There is no evidence before the EI Court to hold that the establishment of the applicant and the establishment of the 3rd opposite party are different.
The EI Court entered certain findings even without any evidence.

The learned counsel invited my attention to the findings of the EI court that the 3rd opposite party - employer employed a new set of employees after taking possession of the premises and that the applicant had no control or employment relation with the employees hired by the 3 rd opposite party.
According to the learned counsel, these findings are made on the basis of a mere assumption.
4. True, there was no evidence before the EI court that the employees employed by the applicant and the 3 rd opposite party are different.

But the facts remain that the applicant INS.APP NO. 15 OF 2025 2025:KER:74841 had produced Ext.A2, a lease agreement by which the applicant leased the premises to the 3 rd opposite party with effect from 22.10.2012.
It is in evidence that the 3 rd opposite party obtained a new Food and Safety license as Ext.A3 for the establishment.
The EI Court considered these two documents and arrived at a finding that the establishment that was run by the applicant and the establishment presently run by the 3 rd opposite party are different.

The EI court relied on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangh v. National Textile Corporation [(1996) 1 SCC 313], in which it is held that mere continuation of business in the same premises or similarity in the name does not make two establishments legally identical unless there is continuity in management, control, or employment.

entities.text: Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangh v. National Textile Corporation [(1996) 1 SCC 313]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of the counsel is that the applicant is the principal employer of the 3rd opposite party.

When the applicant had leased out the entire premises to the 3 rd opposite party, and the 3rd opposite party started functioning in the The Deputy Director vs Mr. K.Vantony on 9 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145467155/
2 establishment after taking a new Food INS.APP NO. 15 OF 2025 2025:KER:74841 and Safety license, it could not be said that the applicant is the principal employer of the 3 rd opposite party.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no evidence before the Commissioner that the applicant retains control over the establishment run by the 3 rd opposite party.
In such a situation, I do not find any perversity in the appreciation of evidence as well as the finding of the EI Court.
Only if there is any perversity in the appreciation of evidence and findings, this Court can entertain an appeal formulating the substantial question of law.
I do not find any ground or reason to interfere.
Accordingly, this appeal is dismissed.
